title: SDC's acquisition by Netcompany moved a member-owned banking cooperative inside a listed competitor
content:
SDC has been acquired by Netcompany. The research frames the change in structural terms rather than as a headline: a member-owned banking cooperative was absorbed by a listed competitor. Its recorded vertical scope is banking only.

Ownership form is decision-relevant here because it determines who can say yes. A cooperative is accountable to the member institutions it serves, whereas a listed acquirer answers to its shareholders and consolidates platform choices at group level. After an absorption of this kind the platform decision may well no longer sit with the entity named on the row, which is enough to make outreach into SDC itself uncertain until the current structure is confirmed.

Everything else on the row is weaker than that. It is a provisional v2 tail entry, rescored mechanically on size and slot occupancy, never scored on v3, with an OSS-portfolio screen still outstanding — so the acquisition is not just the most recent fact on the record, it is very nearly the only researched one.
